records.question: What is the daily room rent sub-limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The daily room rent sub‑limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is Rs. 7,500 per day. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What is the ICU or ICCU daily charges limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Under Apex Health Shield Version 2, there is **no sub‑limit for ICU/ICCU charges** – the policy covers the actual charges up to the Sum Insured. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How many days of pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Pre‑hospitalisation expenses are covered for **60 days prior to admission** under Apex Health Shield Version 2[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How many days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Post‑hospitalisation expenses are covered for **90 days following discharge** under Apex Health Shield Version 2[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the road ambulance limit per hospitalisation under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The road ambulance limit per hospitalisation under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 3,500** per hospitalisation. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What is the coverage limit for AYUSH treatments under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The coverage limit for AYUSH treatments under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **up to 100 % of the Sum Insured**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What is the coverage limit for day care procedures under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The coverage limit for day‑care procedures under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **up to the Sum Insured** for all day‑care procedures (initial 30 days) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the annual limit for organ donor expenses in the benefits table of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The annual limit for organ donor expenses in the benefits table of Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 2,00,000 per policy year** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the daily hospital cash allowance and maximum days covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The daily hospital cash allowance under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 2,000 per day**, and it can be claimed for a **maximum of 15 days** per admission. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What waiting period applies to organ donor expenses in the inpatient schedule of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for organ donor expenses under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **12 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What waiting period applies to the daily hospital cash allowance in the inpatient schedule of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The daily hospital cash allowance is subject to an **initial waiting period of 30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the initial waiting period for illnesses other than accidental injury under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The initial waiting period for illnesses other than accidental bodily injury under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for cataract surgery under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for cataract surgery under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **12 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for hernia and piles under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for hernia and piles under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **24 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for Benign Prostatic Hypertrophy (BPH) under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for Benign Prostatic Hypertrophy (BPH) under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **24 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: What is the waiting period for joint replacement surgery under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for joint replacement surgery (unless accidental) under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **24 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases declared at inception under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the monetary capping limit per eye for cataract surgery under Clause 3.4 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The monetary capping limit per eye for cataract surgery under Clause 3.4 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 60,000 per eye** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What are the base Sum Insured options available under Care Wellness Silver?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Silver plan offers two base Sum Insured options: Rs. 5 Lakhs and Rs. 10 Lakhs. [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What are the base Sum Insured options available under Care Wellness Gold?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Gold plan offers two base Sum Insured choices: Rs. 25 Lakhs and Rs. 50 Lakhs [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: How often is the annual health check-up covered under Care Wellness Silver?
records.answer: The annual health check‑up for the Care Wellness Silver plan is covered **once per year**[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: How often is the annual health check-up covered under Care Wellness Gold?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Gold plan provides coverage for an annual health check‑up **twice per year**[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: What is the maximum wellness renewal discount based on steps for Care Wellness Silver?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Silver plan offers a wellness renewal discount of up to 10 % based on steps [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What is the maximum wellness renewal discount based on steps for Care Wellness Gold?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Gold plan offers a wellness renewal discount of up to 20 % based on steps taken [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: Is worldwide emergency cover included in Care Wellness Silver?
records.answer: No. The Care Wellness Silver plan does not include worldwide emergency cover; it is only provided with the Gold plan [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What is the coverage limit for worldwide emergency cover under Care Wellness Gold?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Gold plan includes worldwide emergency cover with a limit of up to $50,000 [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: What room category entitlement is provided under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The plan provides a **Single Private Room (up to the Sum Insured) with no room‑rent capping** [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: What is the daily ICU charges limit under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Advantage plan does not impose a daily limit on ICU charges; it covers the actual ICU charges incurred, subject only to the overall Sum Insured [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: How many days of pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The policy covers pre‑hospitalisation expenses for **60 days** prior to hospitalisation[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: How many days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: Post‑hospitalisation expenses are covered for **180 days after discharge** under the Care Wellness Advantage plan [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: What is the normal road ambulance coverage limit under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The normal road ambulance coverage under Care Wellness Advantage is up to Rs. 5,000 per hospitalisation[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: What is the air ambulance limit for the Gold variant under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The Gold variant provides air‑ambulance coverage up to **Rs. 5 Lakhs** per hospitalisation[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: What is the lump-sum benefit payable for Cancer of Specified Severity under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The lump‑sum benefit for Cancer of Specified Severity is **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured**[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What survival period is required to claim for Cancer of Specified Severity under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider requires a survival period of **30 days** to claim for Cancer of Specified Severity [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What benefit is payable for First Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction) under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The rider pays a lump‑sum benefit equal to **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for a First Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction) [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What survival period is required for a First Heart Attack claim under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The rider requires the insured to survive 30 days after a diagnosis of a First Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction) to be eligible for the benefit [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What is the lump-sum payout for Open Chest CABG under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The lump‑sum payout for Open Chest CABG is **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured**[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What is the benefit payable for Kidney Failure Requiring Dialysis under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider pays a lump‑sum benefit equal to **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for Kidney Failure Requiring Dialysis[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What survival period is required for Major Organ or Bone Marrow Transplant under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The rider requires a 30‑day survival period for a Major Organ / Bone Marrow Transplant claim [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What is the commission percentage for the Silver tier in the Internal Agent Guide?
records.answer: The commission for the Silver tier is 7 % [AGENT_GUIDE_FAKE p.1].

records.question: How is Inpatient Hospitalisation defined in Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Inpatient Hospitalisation is defined as admission into a Hospital for a minimum contiguous period of 24 consecutive hours[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: What is the minimum bed requirement for a Hospital in towns with a population over 10,000 under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The policy defines a Hospital as an institution that must have **at least 15 in‑patient beds in towns with a population of more than 10,000**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: What is the lookback time window for Pre-existing Disease (PED) diagnosis in Apex Health Shield Version 2 definitions?
records.answer: The definition of Pre‑existing Disease (PED) in Apex Health Shield Version 2 states that it includes any condition for which the insured person had signs, symptoms, a diagnosis, or received medical advice or treatment **within 36 months prior to policy inception**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: What is the duration of the Free-Look Period defined in Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The Free‑Look Period in Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **15 days** from the date the policy schedule is received [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: What is the definition of Grace Period under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The Grace Period is defined as “the specified period of 30 days immediately following the premium due date during which a payment can be made to maintain policy continuity.” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1]

records.question: Is cosmetic surgery covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Cosmetic surgery is not covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2; it is expressly excluded except when it is required as reconstructive surgery following an accidental bodily injury[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

records.question: Are claims for self-inflicted injury or suicide attempt payable under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: No. Under Apex Health Shield Version 2, claims that arise directly or indirectly from intentional self‑inflicted injury or a suicide attempt are expressly excluded and are “strictly non‑payable” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

records.question: What maternity benefit coverage is provided under Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 provides a maternity benefit that covers inpatient medical expenses for maternity, including normal or cesarean delivery, up to Rs. 50,000 per delivery. This benefit becomes available after a 24‑month waiting period and is limited to a maximum of two deliveries per policy [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

records.question: Under what condition is dental treatment covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Dental treatment or surgery is covered only when it requires hospitalisation that arises **solely from an accidental injury**; otherwise it is excluded. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Are weight loss treatments and bariatric surgery covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Weight‑loss treatments, including bariatric surgery, are specifically listed as exclusions in the policy. Therefore, they are **not covered** under Apex Health Shield Version 2. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Are hospital admissions primarily for diagnostic evaluations covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Hospital admissions that are made mainly for diagnostic, radiological or laboratory examinations without any active inpatient medical treatment are excluded under Apex Health Shield Version 2 [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

records.question: How much advance notice is required for planned hospitalisation under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The insured (or their representative) must give the insurer at least 48 hours’ notice before a planned admission at a network hospital [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: When must notice of emergency hospitalisation be provided under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Notice of an emergency hospitalisation must be given within 24 hours of the emergency admission or before discharge, whichever occurs first [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: Within how many days after discharge must claim documents be submitted under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The claim documents must be submitted within **30 days of discharge** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: What mandatory co-payment applies to senior citizens aged 65 and above under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Under Apex Health Shield Version 2, the mandatory co‑payment for insured persons who are 65 years old or older is reduced to **10 % of each admissible claim**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: What is the cumulative bonus percentage increase per claim-free year under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The base Sum Insured increases by **20 % for each claim‑free policy year** under Apex Health Shield Version 2 [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: What is the maximum cumulative bonus limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The policy caps the cumulative bonus at 100 % of the base Sum Insured [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: What is the expense limit for living organ donor harvesting under Clause 6.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The expense limit for hospitalisation costs incurred for organ‑donor harvesting from a living donor is Rs. 2,00,000 under Clause 6.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: Does Care Wellness Advantage require a co-payment for senior citizens entering the policy?
records.answer: Care Wellness Advantage does **not** require a co‑payment for senior citizens (or any other age) when they enter the policy; the plan provides “complete freedom from co‑payments regardless of entry age”[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases under the Care Wellness Advantage plan is 36 months of continuous coverage [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period and sub-limit for cataract surgery under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The Care Wellness Advantage policy provides coverage for cataract surgery after a waiting period of **24 months**, with a **sub‑limit of Rs 50,000 per eye**[CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.3].

records.question: How can a policyholder cancel their policy during the free-look period under Care Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The policyholder can cancel the Care Wellness Advantage policy during the free‑look period by sending a written notice to the insurer within the 15‑day free‑look window that starts from the date the policy is delivered [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.4].

records.question: What is the initial waiting period for the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider has an initial waiting period of 90 days from inception. [​SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2]

records.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing critical conditions under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider imposes a 48‑month waiting period for pre‑existing critical conditions [​SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what minimum duration defines Inpatient Hospitalisation on Page 1, and what daily room rent limit applies on Page 2?
records.answer:
The policy defines **Inpatient Hospitalisation** as an admission that lasts **at least 24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

For Version 2, the **daily room‑rent allowance** is **Rs 7,500 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the Pre-existing Disease definition time window on Page 1 correspond to the PED waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The policy defines a pre‑existing disease as any condition that showed signs, symptoms, diagnosis, medical advice or treatment within **36 months before the policy started** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The waiting period for claims arising from pre‑existing diseases is also set at **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the time window used in the definition (36 months prior to inception) directly matches the 36‑month waiting period required before a pre‑existing disease claim becomes admissible.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the initial waiting period for day care procedures on Page 2 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The policy sets a 30‑day initial waiting period for day‑care procedures (listed under “Day Care Procedures” on page 2) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
The general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is also 30 days (shown in the “Initial Waiting Period” table on page 3) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Therefore, the waiting period for day‑care procedures is the same as the general initial waiting period—both are 30 days.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the organ donor limit in the benefits table on Page 2 align with the organ donor support clause on Page 6?
records.answer:
The benefits table on Page 2 lists **Organ Donor Expenses** as “Covered up to **Rs 2,00,000 per policy year**” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  

The specific organ‑donor support clause on Page 6 states that “hospitalisation expenses incurred for organ donation harvesting from a living donor are payable up to an **enhanced limit of Rs 2,00,000**” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].  

Thus, the limit shown in the benefits table (Rs 2,00,000 per policy year) is consistent with, and reinforced by, the detailed clause that also caps organ‑donor expenses at Rs 2,00,000.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the accidental bodily injury exception to the waiting period on Page 3 relate to the reconstructive cosmetic surgery clause on Page 4?
records.answer:
In Version 2 the waiting‑period table states that the 30‑day initial waiting period applies to “all illnesses **except accidental bodily injury**” — so injuries that are accidental are not subject to that waiting period [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

The cosmetic‑surgery exclusion on Page 4 adds that cosmetic or aesthetic procedures are excluded **unless** they are required as reconstructive surgery **following accidental bodily injury** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  

Together, these provisions mean that a claim for reconstructive cosmetic surgery that results from an accidental bodily injury is not subject to the 30‑day waiting period and is covered (i.e., not excluded) under the policy.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the maternity benefit waiting period under Section 4.3 on Page 4 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The maternity benefit under Section 4.3 is subject to a **24‑month waiting period** before any maternity‑related expenses are payable [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  

The policy’s general “initial waiting period” for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Therefore, the maternity waiting period (24 months) is considerably longer than the standard initial waiting period of 30 days.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what notice is required for planned admission on Page 5, and what minimum hospital stay is required on Page 1?
records.answer:
The policy requires that the insured or their representative give the insurer **at least 48 hours’ notice before a planned admission** at a network hospital [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].  

For a hospital stay to qualify as inpatient hospitalisation, the admission must be for **a minimum contiguous period of 24 hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the Free-Look Period duration defined on Page 1, and what refund terms apply under Section 5.3 on Page 5?
records.answer:
The policy defines the Free‑Look Period as **15 days** from the date the policyholder receives the policy document [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

Under Section 5.3, the free‑look period is also stated to be **15 days** from receipt of the policy schedule, and if no claim is made during that time the premium is refunded **subject to minimal administrative charges** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: In Care Wellness Advantage, what Sum Insured options are offered for Gold on Page 1, and what room category entitlement applies on Page 2?
records.answer:
The Gold variant of Care Wellness Advantage provides two Sum‑Insured choices: Rs. 25 Lakhs and Rs. 50 Lakhs [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

For inpatient hospitalisation, the entitlement is a **Single Private Room (up to the Sum Insured) with no room‑rent capping** [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: In Care Wellness Advantage, what worldwide emergency coverage is provided for Gold on Page 1, and what air ambulance limit is provided on Page 2?
records.answer:
The Gold version of Care Wellness Advantage includes worldwide emergency coverage of up to **$50,000** [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].  

For air‑ambulance services, the Gold plan provides a limit of **Rs. 5 Lakhs** per hospitalisation [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: In Care Wellness Advantage, how does the free co-payment highlight on Page 1 compare to the pre-existing disease waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The plan offers “complete freedom from co‑payments” right from the start of the policy — the benefit is available immediately on Day 1 [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].  
In contrast, coverage for pre‑existing diseases does not begin until after a 36‑month continuous‑coverage waiting period [CARE_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.3].  

Thus, the co‑payment exemption is effective immediately, whereas the pre‑existing disease benefit requires a three‑year waiting period.

records.question: How does the daily room rent sub-limit compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
Version 2 raises the daily room‑rent sub‑limit to Rs 7,500 per day, whereas Version 1 limits it to Rs 5,000 per day. This means the allowable room‑rent amount per day is Rs 2,500 higher in the newer version.  

- Version 2 room‑rent sub‑limit: Rs 7,500 per day [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]  
- Version 1 room‑rent sub‑limit: Rs 5,000 per day [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2]

records.question: How do the ICU charges limits differ between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
Version 1 places a specific sub‑limit on ICU/ICCU charges of **Rs 10,000 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2].  
Version 2 removes that sub‑limit, allowing the actual ICU/ICCU charges to be covered **up to the overall Sum Insured** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does pre-hospitalisation expense coverage duration compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
Version 2 extends the pre‑hospitalisation benefit to 60 days before admission, whereas Version 1 limits it to 30 days before admission. Thus, the coverage duration for pre‑hospitalisation expenses is twice as long in Apex Health Shield Version 2 as it is in Version 1.  

- Pre‑hospitalisation cover – 60 days prior to admission (Version 2) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]  
- Pre‑hospitalisation cover – 30 days prior to admission (Version 1) [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2]

records.question: How does post-hospitalisation expense coverage duration compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
Version 2 extends the post‑hospitalisation coverage period to 90 days after discharge, whereas Version 1 provides coverage for only 60 days after discharge. Thus, the post‑hospitalisation expense coverage duration is 30 days longer in Version 2 than in Version 1.  

- V1 post‑hospitalisation: 60 days [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2]  
- V2 post‑hospitalisation: 90 days [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How does the road ambulance limit per hospitalisation compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
Version 2 provides a higher road‑ambulance allowance than Version 1.  
- In Version 2 the limit is **Rs 3,500 per hospitalisation**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
- In Version 1 the limit is **Rs 2,000 per hospitalisation**[APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2].  

Thus, the road‑ambulance limit per hospitalisation increases by Rs 1,500 in Version 2 compared with Version 1.

records.question: How did the waiting period for cataract surgery change from Version 1 to Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer: The waiting period for cataract surgery was shortened. In Version 1 the policy required a 24‑month waiting period for cataract surgery and treatment [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3]. In Version 2 this waiting period was reduced to 12 months [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: How did the cataract surgery monetary sub-limit per eye change between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer: The cataract‑surgery sub‑limit was raised from **Rs 40,000 per eye** in Version 1 to **Rs 60,000 per eye** in Version 2, an increase of Rs 20,000 per eye[APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3][APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.answer: Version 2 of Apex Health Shield has the shorter waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception (36 months) compared with Version 1’s 48‑month period [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3].
